newsitem.title: ITALY: Space insurance capacity soars - Generali.
newsitem.headline: Space insurance capacity soars - Generali.

text.p: Capacity in the space insurance market has soared to $850 million from $550 million in 1995 as new players enter the market attracted by potential high premiums, Italian insurer Generali said.

However, the increase could threaten the future stability of the market because of a lack of expertise, general deputy general manager Benito Pagnanelli told its biennial space insurance conference on Thursday.

"We are dealing with operators who are sustained by large capital and who enter the market with considerable capacity. They have the typical characteristics of those insurers who offer but an opportunistic presence, based more on fortune and gambling than on a will to remain in the market," Pagnanelli said.
"Often they charge inadequate premiums and expose themselves to high participation shares, thereby reducing the negotiating power of the more experienced companies."

"We must take heed, and make sure the high capacity existing today shouldn't be the cause in the future -- if results should worsen -- of a shrinking market that is unable to cover the mounting cost of insurance requirements in the space sector," he said.
He reminded delegates that in 1985 and 1986 capacity fell below $100 million after some poor years, sparking a rise of 33 percent in insurance rates.
Pagnanelli said the loss rate had been relatively high in 1996, but did not compare with the "annus terribilis" of 1994, when space insurers paid out around $770 million.

Generali figures showed that the maximum insured value of satellites has increased, now exceeding $300 million each, as had the cost of launch insurance, now averaging $500 million. Net premiums for 1995 and 1996 went up accordingly.
The space insurance industry has collected around $4.8 billion in premiums since 1984, according to Generali, while around $900 million has been paid out in claims.
Europe held 73 percent of the market in 1996, with Generali the biggest player with capacity of $110 million. The U.S. holds 17 percent of the market, and the rest of the world 10 percent.
